public_rationale: CNBC's September 27, 2024 estimates imply about $27.28 billion in expenses at $11.6 billion in revenue if the estimated spending ratio remains fixed [e1]. The Financial Times reported on June 15, 2026 that OpenAI recorded about $13 billion in revenue and $34 billion in spending during 2025 [e2]. The revenue target was exceeded, but these reports do not establish that the assumed cost ratio persisted on a comparable expense basis [e1, e2]. The conditional forecast remains unresolved.
limitations: The hypothetical calculation does not establish actual 2025 expenses.
The original estimates, later spending figures and losses adjusted for non-cash expenses are not reconciled.
Annual totals do not establish expenses incurred when revenue reached $11.6 billion.

from_speaker: At the current cost of revenue
our_interpretation: Read this as a conditional projection using the surrounding $2.35 of spending per dollar of revenue.
In context, cost of revenue means the broader spending measure used to infer that ratio, not necessarily the accounting line called cost of revenue.
The forecast requires both reaching the revenue target and retaining a comparable cost-to-revenue relationship. The multiplication alone does not demonstrate those conditions occurred.
Use calendar-year realized revenue rather than an annualized revenue run rate.
criteria.support_condition: If both conditions occurred, comparable 2025 expenses associated with reaching the revenue target exceeded $27 billion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: If both conditions occurred, comparable expenses associated with reaching the revenue target were no more than $27 billion.
